learningObjective: Reason about when kernel launch overhead dominates and what mitigations exist.

canonicalClaims.claim: When per-kernel duration is comparable to or smaller than the ~5–10 μs launch overhead, wall time is dominated by CPU-side launches; CUDA Graphs and kernel fusion are the standard mitigations.
conditions: Loop dispatches many short kernels (< 20 μs each).
Baseline uses one launch per kernel call.
No implicit graph capture or persistent-kernel scheme.
nonImplications: Does not imply CUDA Graphs is free; graph construction has its own cost and constraints.
Does not imply fusion is always beneficial (register pressure, occupancy trade-offs).

misconceptions.claim: Asynchronous kernel launches eliminate launch overhead.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Async launch decouples CPU wait from kernel completion but the launch API still consumes CPU time (~5–10 μs) and paces the launch stream.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA Graphs eliminates launch overhead entirely.
misconceptions.whyWrong: CUDA Graphs amortizes per-kernel API overhead across a single graph-launch, but graph instantiation and update have their own costs, and dynamic shapes may force re-capture.

misconceptions.claim: Kernel fusion is always beneficial for performance.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Over-fusion can increase register pressure and reduce occupancy or force spills; fusion is a case-by-case optimization.

implementationFacts: Launch overhead ~ 5–10 μs per cudaLaunchKernel (recent drivers).
CUDA Graphs replay overhead ~ 1–2 μs per graph launch after capture.
Kernel fusion also reduces HBM traffic when producer-consumer share operands.
performanceScenarios: LLM decode dispatches many short kernels per token; CUDA Graphs and fused attention kernels are standard mitigations.
